package_info.package_versions: 7.69.0 up to and including 8.3.0 (CVE-2023-38545); 7.9.1 up to and including 8.3.0 (CVE-2023-38546)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of curl/libcurl contain a heap overflow vulnerability (CVE-2023-38545) that can be triggered when connecting to an attacker-controlled HTTP server over a SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolving (socks5h://). This allows an attacker to potentially achieve denial of service or remote code execution by exploiting improper buffer handling in the state machine logic.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when making a network request via SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolution)
execution_context.file_location: libcurl source code (SOCKS5 state machine, e.g., url.c or socks.c)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a hostname longer than 255 bytes is encountered in a SOCKS5 proxy connection, the code attempts to fall back to local resolution but later incorrectly constructs a protocol frame, copying the long hostname into a small heap buffer, resulting in a heap overflow.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code fails to properly handle the case where a hostname exceeds the SOCKS5 protocol limit, leading to a buffer overflow.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would strictly enforce the 255-byte limit and reject or truncate overlong hostnames, not attempt to process them further.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code would handle protocol limits gracefully, never allowing buffer overflows.
key_indicators: Improper bounds checking on hostname length
Heap buffer overflow due to unchecked copy
Protocol fallback logic that does not prevent unsafe memory operations

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when following HTTP redirects from attacker-controlled server)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Location: https://aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/ (host name can be extended up to 64KB)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the client receives an HTTP 30x redirect with a Location header containing an excessively long hostname, which is then processed by the vulnerable SOCKS5 state machine, triggering the heap overflow.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of an extremely long hostname in the Location header is abnormal and designed to trigger memory handling bugs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTTP redirects use valid, reasonably sized hostnames; overlong hostnames should be rejected.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for such long hostnames in redirects.
key_indicators: Interaction with SOCKS5 proxy using remote resolution

attack_chain.action: Attacker sets up a malicious HTTP server to issue a redirect with an overlong hostname in the Location header.
attack_chain.leads_to: Client processes the redirect and attempts to connect to the new hostname via SOCKS5 proxy.

attack_chain.action: Client (curl/libcurl) processes the redirect and attempts to connect to the attacker-supplied hostname using a SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolution (socks5h://).
attack_chain.leads_to: Heap buffer overflow is triggered in the client, potentially leading to denial of service or remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: SOCKS5 proxy usage with remote hostname resolution (socks5h:// or CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME)
HTTP redirects with extremely long hostnames (>255 bytes)
Heap buffer overflows or segmentation faults in curl/libcurl processes
network_indicators: Outbound connections to SOCKS5 proxies using the socks5h:// scheme
HTTP 30x redirects with Location headers containing hostnames longer than 255 bytes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for use of the socks5h:// scheme in curl/libcurl invocations, either via command-line flags (--socks5-hostname, -x socks5h://) or API usage (CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME). Inspect HTTP traffic for 30x redirects with abnormally long hostnames in the Location header. Watch for segmentation faults or abnormal crashes in curl/libcurl processes, especially when interacting with SOCKS5 proxies. Use static analysis to flag code that sets CURLOPT_PROXYTYPE to CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME or uses socks5h:// in proxy settings.
